question_text: Were GoFundMe Pro and DonorPerfect hacked?
answer_text: Yes, by both companies' own accounts: GoFundMe says an unauthorized party accessed GoFundMe Pro data; DonorPerfect says it found unauthorized activity and went offline. Who did it, and whether one attacker, is not established.
label: Confirmed
what_would_settle_it: Published forensic findings from either company, or a law enforcement statement.

question_text: Was personal data taken from GoFundMe Pro?
answer_text: Yes, per GoFundMe: names, postal addresses, phone numbers and, for some people, dates of birth. How many people is not published.
label: Confirmed
what_would_settle_it: A published count, or a state regulator filing with one.

question_text: Was customer data taken from DonorPerfect?
answer_text: Not established. DonorPerfect says it does not yet know what, if anything, was taken.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: A DonorPerfect statement or notice saying what data was affected.

question_text: Were card numbers or bank details taken?
answer_text: GoFundMe says no full card numbers, security codes or bank account details were accessed, and no donor credentials, "at this time". That is its own statement, not independently checked. DonorPerfect has not said.
label: Reported
what_would_settle_it: Final findings from GoFundMe's investigation, or an independent review.

answer_text: Mostly no. It has restored the application in stages since Nov 14, but its API and mobile app were still unavailable on Nov 21, and it has no reliable date for the rest.
label: Confirmed
what_would_settle_it: DonorPerfect marking the API and mobile app restored.

question_text: Did AI bots carry out the attacks?
answer_text: Reported, as a DonorPerfect claim only. The company says it has a lot of evidence and that the bots came in through its marketing website. No outside expert has reviewed it.
label: Reported
what_would_settle_it: A published forensic report, or independent review of the evidence.

question_text: Was it the same attacker at both companies, and who was it?
answer_text: Not established. Neither company says it was the same attacker as the other, and no source names a group.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: An official finding, or a credible independent report linking them.

answer_text: Salesforce says no: it disabled the GoFundMe Pro connected app after suspicious use of access tokens and says it was not a flaw in the Salesforce platform. We found that only as a statement quoted in press.
label: Reported
what_would_settle_it: A public Salesforce or GoFundMe account of how the tokens were obtained.

question_text: Were funds diverted from a platform?
answer_text: Unverified. One anonymous account in one outlet; neither company says money was taken.
label: Unverified
what_would_settle_it: A company, regulator or law enforcement statement.

question_text: Is this connected to the other outages this month?
answer_text: Not established. Fortune lists them together but says this case was different because the company confirmed unauthorized activity.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: An official or independent finding linking the incidents.
